thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING on-call: cross-zone networking anomaly observed — elevated p99/TLS handshake failures affecting streaming responses in prod (us-west-2 <-> us-east-1). Auto-page to SRE.

maria: I’m on it. seeing p95 ~450ms -> 1.2s and p99 jumping to 2.6s across multiple routes. Streaming stall rate ~14% for live chat routes.

ajay: observed spike coincident with a DNS change from partner NAT provider at 04:10 UTC. cdn-egress metrics show increased RTT and retransmits on cross-az paths.

kevin: tcpdump on host backends shows intermittent packet loss 0.5-1.2% between AZ-b and AZ-c via our NAT pool. Also seeing many TLS handshake renegotiations (RSA->ECDHE resumption failures).

sophia: customer-impact: AcmeMedia sessions facing rebuffering and delayed tokens; support has 6 active severity-2 tickets. Estimated affected qps ~1200 (5% of total).

maria: paging triage checklist: 1) confirm blast radius, 2) mitigate traffic path, 3) collect pcap/logs, 4) coordinate cloud provider/partner.

kevin: blast radius: cross-zone only (intra-AZ ok). Hosted endpoints in us-west-2 show normal latency to local clients; cross-zone tail suffers. NAT gateway metrics show CPU, conntrack near saturation for a small subset of IPs.

ajay: quick mitigation idea: prefer AZ-local egress for streaming sessions via routing policy override for affected customers; fallback to local model replicas. Can push a temporary traffic-policy tag.

maria: do it. @deploy-bot can we apply an emergency routing policy to prefer AZ-local egress for routes matching /streaming/*? Keep 30m TTL.

deploy-bot: received emergency job request: apply-policy streaming-az-local-override -> staging validation passed -> deploying to prod canaries (5%).

maria: ramp canary to 30% for affected accounts, watch p99 and stall rate.

kevin: concurrently opening ticket with cloud NAT provider: ticket #CLD-78321 — sending pcap, conntrack dumps, and ASN traces. Noted that a subset of NAT IPs are showing abnormal retransmit counters.

ajay: running a rolling restart of the NAT proxy fleet in az-b to clear conntrack. Command:
```
for i in $(seq 1 12); do ssh nat-proxy-$i 'sudo systemctl restart nat-proxy && sleep 10'; done
```

maria: monitoring: after routing override + nat-proxy restarts p95 dropped to 220ms, p99 to 480ms for canary traffic. streaming stalls down from 14% -> 3.5% on canary. :thumbsup:

sophia: escalate to CS: update customers (AcmeMedia) with ETA 60m, mention we applied temporary routing to reduce impact and are working with provider on root cause.

kevin: provider responded: they see backend packet drops tied to one peering router in us-east-1. They will fail over path and replace ASIC. ETA 40 min.

maria: good. we should still prepare rollback plan in case the override causes other issues. Runbook: revert-policy streaming-az-local-override -> command `routectl revert streaming-az-local-override`

ajay: note: observed TLS handshake spike was likely due to SYN retransmits causing handshake timeouts and forcing full handshakes instead of resumption — will enable stricter keepalive and increase connection pool sizes on frontends temporarily:
```
nginx: keepalive_timeout 75s;
upstream { keepalive 1024; }
```

maria: changed nginx keepalive on streaming frontends in prod (hot patch), no restart, reload config. monitor for 5m.

kevin: after provider failover and our hotfixes: cross-zone retransmits down to 0.08%, p99 for streaming routes back to ~310ms, stalls ~1.2%.

sophia: support: pushing a note to affected tickets: "We applied routing and connection fixes; provider performed peering failover; we continue to monitor. If you still see rebuffering please attach a session id."

maria: on-call handoff inbound: @ops-pager I’ll hand to you for postmortem & RCA capture at 05:30 UTC. Current status: degraded->recovering.

ops-pager: taking over. key artifacts to collect: 1) pcap slices (pre/during/post) from nat-proxies, 2) conntrack histograms, 3) TLS handshake logs, 4) provider ASN/peering events, 5) routing policy change log.

maria: attaching quick logs snippets: `tcpdump -w /tmp/trace-azb.pcap 'host 10.12.34.5 and port 443'` and `conntrack -L | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l` returned spikes up to 160k.

ajay: also enable debug for our streaming router at level DEBUG for 30m: `/api/ops/debug?component=stream-router&level=DEBUG&ttl=30m`

ops-pager: noted. I’ll file the incident doc and tag network, infra, and provider fields. SLA impact: some customers breached p99 latency SLO for ~24 mins. Open action items assigned.

maria: final note for timeline: 04:08 UTC first metric deviation; 04:10 UTC provider DNS change; 04:12 UTC incident page; 04:16 UTC routing override applied; 04:29 UTC provider failover complete; 04:40 UTC p99 recovered below SLO.

ops-pager: copying this thread to incidents channel summary. Will schedule RCA meeting tomorrow 14:00 UTC. :calendar:

maria: thanks all. leaving notes in runbook and passing to ops-pager.

incident-bot: Incident updated: status -> recovering, severity -> sev2, incident_id -> INC-2026-1593.

ops-pager: closing handoff. i will own the postmortem and coordinate with provider for permanent mitigation (expand NAT pool + peering redundancy).

sophia: tagging support to follow up with affected customers, include timeline and mitigation steps.

maria: resuming normal monitoring, stay tuned if anything else pops up.

(End of thread)
